claims.text: The initial refractory high-entropy alloy has a BCC solid-solution microstructure.
The initial alloy is a NbMoCrTi-based variant with minimal or no aluminum.
The initial alloy exhibits moderate high-temperature oxygen resistance.
Adding 2–5 at% aluminum will enable formation of a continuous, adherent Al2O3 layer during high-temperature exposure.
The aluminum-containing alloy will develop a continuous, slow-growing, and adherent alumina scale at approximately 800 °C in air.
At high temperature, added aluminum preferentially segregates to the alloy surface.
Surface-enriched aluminum reacts with ambient oxygen to form a dense alumina scale.
The alumina scale acts as a barrier to further oxygen ingress.
Blocking oxygen ingress reduces overall oxidation and delays scale breakaway relative to an alloy lacking sufficient aluminum.
After 100 hours in static laboratory air at 800 °C, aluminum addition will reduce mass gain by at least 50% relative to the untreated alloy.
The aluminum-enhanced alloy will form a thinner and more protective oxide scale than the untreated alloy.
The aluminum-enhanced alloy will better preserve its microstructural integrity during oxidation.
Under the same exposure, the untreated alloy forms a thicker, more porous, and less protective oxide scale.
The untreated alloy's oxide scale causes greater oxygen uptake and may spall.
The oxidation-resistance benefit is expected primarily near 800 °C.
At temperatures at or above 900 °C, or considerably below 800 °C, altered alumina formation kinetics or stability may change the benefit.
The optimal aluminum concentration and its interactions with the alloy's other elements remain undetermined.
The effects of aluminum addition on mechanical properties and long-term phase stability are uncertain.
The intervention can be tested by comparing baseline and 2–5 at% Al-modified samples during identical 800 °C, 100-hour static-air exposures.
Failure to obtain both a statistically significant mass-gain reduction of at least 50% and a continuous, predominantly Al2O3 scale is specified as falsifying the hypothesis.
